member.name: T:Meziantou.Framework.RobotsTxt.RobotsFile
member.summary: Represents a parsed robots.txt file.

remarks.para: The parser is lenient: unknown directives and malformed lines are skipped rather than throwing, matching the behaviour of most web crawlers. Each skipped line is recorded in so callers can audit file quality.
Supported directives: User-agent, Allow, Disallow, Crawl-delay, and Sitemap.
Path patterns in Allow and Disallow directives support Google's wildcard extensions: * matches any sequence of characters, and a trailing $ anchors the pattern to the end of the path.

member.name: M:Meziantou.Framework.RobotsTxt.RobotsFile.GetGroup(System.String)
member.summary: Returns the that best matches the given .

remarks.para: An exact (case-insensitive) match takes precedence over a catch-all (*) group. Returns when no group matches.

When several groups declare the selected user-agent token, their rules are merged into a single group, as required by RFC 9309 section 2.2.1. The merged group is not one of the instances in : it lists the union of the declared tokens, the rules of every contributing group in file order, and the first Crawl-delay that was specified. When exactly one group matches, that instance is returned as-is.

member.name: M:Meziantou.Framework.RobotsTxt.RobotsGroup.IsAllowed(System.String)
member.summary: Determines whether the given is allowed by the rules in this group.

remarks.para: The most specific (longest ) matching rule wins. When two matching rules have equal specificity, takes precedence.
An empty Disallow path is treated as "allow all" and only matches when no other rule matches. If no rule matches the path, access is allowed.

member.param: The URL path (and optional query string) to check.
member.returns: if access is allowed; if it is disallowed.
